title: Electrical Fundamentals: Receptacles and Box Layout
markdown:
# RCS Day 3 - Electrical Fundamentals: Receptacles and Box Layout
CTS Cohort 6 | CTS Day 11 | 2026-07-22 | 10:00 AM-3:00 PM

## Core rule
A professional does not guess. A professional checks, protects, and verifies.

## Big idea
Residential wiring is a controlled path; professionals de-energize, verify, route, terminate, inspect, and document.

## Architecture of the day
| Time | Instructor move |
|---|---|
| 10:00-10:15 | Arrival, PPE, retrieval warm-up |
| 10:15-10:30 | Morning quiz |
| 10:30-10:50 | Quiz review and energy-boundary check |
| 10:50-11:20 | Hot, neutral, and grounding path model |
| 11:20-12:00 | Box-layout and receptacle termination demonstration |
| 12:00-12:30 | Verification ladder guided practice and lab release |
| 12:30-1:00 | Lunch and controlled reset |
| 1:00-2:25 | Two-box, two-receptacle de-energized capstone lab |
| 2:25-2:45 | Visual, tug, continuity, evidence, cleanup |
| 2:45-3:00 | Exit ticket and Day 4 preview |

## Learning targets
- Trace hot, neutral, and equipment-grounding paths in a training circuit
- Lay out two receptacle boxes on the capstone wall
- Prepare and terminate conductors on training receptacles
- Complete visual, mechanical, and continuity checks while de-energized

## Materials and setup
- Six isolated training wall stations; no premises-power connection
- Two device boxes and two training receptacles per student
- Training cable/conductors, grounding hardware, labels, and approved diagrams
- Strippers, hand tools, and manufacturer-directed termination tools
- Meters reserved for de-energized continuity checks
- Eye protection, drilling controls, and evidence devices

## Instructor talking points
- Retrieve PV101 circuit-path and meter habits without assuming field authorization.
- Separate conductor purpose from color shorthand; verify the training diagram.
- Demonstrate box layout, cable protection, jacket entry, conductor length, stripping, clockwise terminal loops, torque-by-manufacturer, and grounding.
- Teach the inspection ladder: de-energized verification, visual check, tug test, continuity check, instructor approval.
- Explain that Oregon-regulated installations require appropriate permits, inspections, and licensed work.
